It operates on air-gapped snapshots with no cloud credentials, no API calls, and no network access.

- [What you just discovered](/docs/labs/case-studies-debrief.md): What the S3 reasoning challenge reveals about the gap between scanning and reasoning.
- [Challenge Setup](/docs/labs/case-studies-setup.md): Download 4 JSON files and try to answer 5 questions about S3 security — no Stave, no AWS account.
- [HackerOne Case Studies](/docs/labs/case-studies.md): 30 real HackerOne bug bounty reports reconstructed as reasoning challenges, grouped by attack pattern.
- [The audit log that watched the front door while the side door stayed open](/docs/labs/case-studies/aws-3021451.md): A CloudTrail reads as fully configured, yet ElastiCache calls through a non-production endpoint generate no log entries at all.
- [The two side doors the audit log was never told about](/docs/labs/case-studies/aws-3022516.md): A correctly configured trail still misses Amazon Forecast calls made through two non-production endpoints the service never delivers to CloudTrail.
- [The upload policy with no destination it would refuse](/docs/labs/case-studies/bcm-764243.md): A presigned POST policy uses an empty starts-with prefix, so any key in the bucket is a legal upload target — can you prove the write scope is unrestricted from the policy alone?
- [The subdomain that pointed at a name anyone could take](/docs/labs/case-studies/bime-121461.md): Reasoning that a live DNS record plus a claimable bucket name is a takeover primitive, even while the page returns a harmless 404.
- [The repository nobody deleted from the install guide](/docs/labs/case-studies/brave-1791558.md): An APT repository bucket was deleted but the DNS name and the community install guide still point at it — can you prove the reference is claimable from the static evidence alone?
- [The install guide that points at a bucket anyone can claim](/docs/labs/case-studies/brave-1835133.md): A 404 today, a trojaned RPM repository tomorrow — can you tell that a harmless dangling reference is one registration away from supply-chain compromise?
- [The metadata door that opened for anyone who asked](/docs/labs/case-studies/dod-2083771.md): Reasoning that an exposed Jenkins console plus IMDSv1 forms a single credential-theft path, not two independent low findings.
- [The government domain pointing at a name up for grabs](/docs/labs/case-studies/dod-918946.md): Reasoning that a dangling .gov CNAME is a high-trust takeover primitive while it still serves a harmless 404.
- [Public read was fine — public listing leaked the whole catalog](/docs/labs/case-studies/greenhouse-819278.md): Marketing assets are public by design, but the same grant also exposes the full inventory — separating intended exposure from disclosure.
- [The widget script that's one bucket registration from XSS](/docs/labs/case-studies/hackerone-1598347.md): A deleted widget bucket plus a live <script> tag — can you see that claiming the name turns a dead reference into attacker JavaScript on the parent domain?
- [The bucket that shipped attachments in the clear](/docs/labs/case-studies/hackerone-43280.md): Both HTTP and HTTPS serve the same objects — can you prove, from the policy alone, that nothing is leaking on the wire?
- [The subdomain an acquisition left pointing at nothing](/docs/labs/case-studies/ibm-2498255.md): A subsidiary's DNS outlived its bucket after a merger — can you tell that an inherited 404 is a branded takeover waiting for someone to claim the name?
- [The website endpoint that would serve anyone's index.html](/docs/labs/case-studies/khanacademy-1777077.md): Reasoning that a dangling website-hosting CNAME is a seamless takeover-and-session-theft primitive while it still returns a 404.
- [The Ingress that rewrote a neighbor's firewall](/docs/labs/case-studies/kubernetes-1238482.md): A controller reconciles security groups from annotations it never checks for ownership — can you spot the cross-tenant write before it happens?
- [The cluster admin keyed to an identifier that isn't a secret](/docs/labs/case-studies/kubernetes-1580493.md): An EKS aws-auth mapping uses the AccessKeyID as the identity and hands it system:masters — turning a public string into full cluster admin.
- [The bucket named private whose objects were public](/docs/labs/case-studies/mapbox-202725.md): Bucket-level config looks locked down, but per-object ACLs make individual objects public — catching exposure the bucket settings hide.
- [The static site that published its own .git history](/docs/labs/case-studies/mozilla-2383486.md): A public bucket serves static content but also exposes a synced .git directory — distinguishing harmless public files from a source-code leak.
- [The payment-processor bucket with two front doors and a fix that only closed one](/docs/labs/case-studies/omise-1474017.md): A CDN origin bucket is opened by both an ACL and a policy — can you tell from the config that fixing one path leaves the other wide open?
- [The bucket labelled internal that handed out a table of contents](/docs/labs/case-studies/shopify-1021906.md): A production API bucket tagged internal grants the public both read and list — can you tell from the config what an attacker can enumerate?
- [The address that pointed at a chair nobody was sitting in](/docs/labs/case-studies/shopify-1295497.md): An EC2 instance was terminated and its Elastic IP released, but the DNS A record still points at the old address — can you prove the record is dangling from the static evidence alone?
- [The public bucket that also handed out its own index](/docs/labs/case-studies/shopify-57505.md): A bucket meant to serve images publicly also grants public listing — telling whether the extra permission is intentional or a leak.
- [The merchant upload that could rewrite any other merchant](/docs/labs/case-studies/shopify-93691.md): A presigned POST policy scopes uploads to a prefix shared by all merchants — can you prove one merchant can overwrite another's files from the policy alone?
- [The upload token that trusted the path it was handed](/docs/labs/case-studies/shopify-94087.md): A presigned URL scoped one prefix too wide lets one tenant write into another tenant's space — isolation that lives in a single Resource string.
- [The remediation that fixed listing and left write wide open](/docs/labs/case-studies/shopify-94502.md): A partial fix removed public listing but left public read and public write via ACL — judging whether remediation is actually complete.
- [The drop box anyone could fill and one stranger could read](/docs/labs/case-studies/shopify-98819.md): Anonymous write via ACL plus cross-account read via policy form a data-injection pipeline that neither setting reveals on its own.
- [The test builds that shipped their own secrets to the public internet](/docs/labs/case-studies/slack-404822.md): A public bucket policy paired with a Public Access Block that blocks nothing — can you tell from the config whether the toggle protects anything?
- [The install command pointing at a bucket someone else could fill](/docs/labs/case-studies/tendermint-1397826.md): Reasoning that a dangling release-bucket CNAME referenced by install docs is a supply-chain takeover primitive while it still returns a 404.
- [The bucket that called itself confidential and then served itself to everyone](/docs/labs/case-studies/uber-361438.md): A bucket tagged confidential carries a policy that grants the whole internet read access — can you prove the contradiction from the static config alone?
- [The upload door that opened onto everyone's room](/docs/labs/case-studies/unikrn-254200.md): A presigned upload policy restricts keys to a prefix shared by every tenant — can you prove the prefix breaks tenant isolation from the policy alone?
- [The chat images anyone could browse, one key at a time](/docs/labs/case-studies/zomato-507097.md): A bucket of user chat images is open by both ACL and policy, with listing on — can you tell from the config that the privacy harm comes from enumeration, not just read?
- [The Five Questions](/docs/labs/case-study-questions.md): Five questions about S3 security to answer from static configuration — before you see what Stave finds.

- [Cognito Unauthenticated S3 Takeover](/docs/labs/cognito-unauthenticated-s3-takeover.md): Detect a Cognito identity pool whose guest role can read and write S3, read the findings, then learn the single most important Stave concept: it evaluates a captured snapshot, so a live fix is invisible until you re-capture.

- [Cross-Account KMS Key Policy & CMK Isolation](/docs/labs/cross-account-kms-key-policy-isolation.md): Detect a KMS key whose policy opens broad, unconditioned cross-account access — a wildcard principal and an excessive sharing blast radius. Read all three findings, learn why exit 3 means success, and fix-then-recapture to green.

- [Docker Scenarios](/docs/labs/docker-scenarios.md)
- [ACL Privilege Escalation](/docs/labs/docker-scenarios/acl-escalation.md): Buckets where ACL grants (WRITEACP, READACP, FULL_CONTROL) enable attackers to modify permissions, enumerate access, or gain complete control -- even when the bucket policy looks clean.
- [ACL-Based Public Write](/docs/labs/docker-scenarios/acl-write.md): User upload bucket where ACL grants write to any authenticated AWS user. The bucket policy looks clean — policy-only scanners miss this entirely.
- [Data Governance and Lifecycle](/docs/labs/docker-scenarios/data-governance.md): Backup bucket missing data classification, lifecycle rules, MFA delete, versioning, and Public Access Block -- a cascade of governance failures that compounds risk.
- [HIPAA Multi-Violation](/docs/labs/docker-scenarios/hipaa-compliance.md): PHI (Protected Health Information) bucket with multiple HIPAA compliance failures: no encryption at rest, no transport encryption, no KMS key management, no access logging, no versioning, no object lock, and no Public Access Block.
- [Public Read via Bucket Policy](/docs/labs/docker-scenarios/public-read.md): Internal analytics data exposed to the internet via Principal: "*" bucket policy with Public Access Block disabled.
- [Security Tool Bypass](/docs/labs/docker-scenarios/tool-blind-spot.md): Buckets that appear safe to tools relying on APIs the bucket policy denies, plus latent public read exposure masked only by Public Access Block.
- [Upload Policy Hardening](/docs/labs/docker-scenarios/upload-hardening.md): Signed upload policies that allow prefix-scoped keys or unrestricted content types, enabling object overwrite and stored XSS attacks.

- [HackerOne Case Challenges](/docs/labs/hackerone.md): 30 real HackerOne bug bounty cases as reasoning challenges — can you find the misconfiguration from static evidence?
- [Building Detection Metrics from Lab Results](/docs/labs/lab-metrics.md): Load CloudGoat lab findings and compute detection metrics, severity breakdowns, and assessment diffs using pkg/stave.
- [Lambda MicroVM Security Labs](/docs/labs/lambda-microvm.md): Eight self-contained labs for the Lambda MicroVM control family.
- [Lab 3B — Trust Policy Over-Broad sts:TagSession (sts:* wildcard)](/docs/labs/lambda-microvm/03b-overbroad-tagsession.md): A least-privilege MicroVM execution role whose trust policy grants sts:TagSession through an sts:* wildcard. The mirror of Lab 3 — there TagSession is missing; here it is present but granted over-broadly. One control fires; scope the actions and re-verify to zero.
- [Lab 1 — Baseline: A Compliant MicroVM](/docs/labs/lambda-microvm/baseline-compliant-microvm.md): Orient yourself in the Lambda MicroVM lab: the 16 built-in CTL.LAMBDA.MICROVM.* controls, the obs.v0.1 shape they read, and the capture → transform → evaluate loop. Build a compliant configuration and watch every control pass.
- [Lab 4 — Compound Path: Graph Reachability](/docs/labs/lambda-microvm/compound-path.md): The finding per-resource scanners structurally cannot see. A MicroVM role reaches a production secret through an assume-role hop — each hop passes its individual check. Soufflé and Z3 compute the reachability; remediation breaks the chain.
- [Lab 6 — Excessive Idle and Runtime](/docs/labs/lambda-microvm/excessive-idle-runtime.md): A MicroVM with maxIdleDurationSeconds and total runtime at the 8-hour ceiling. Two runtime controls fire; lower both within the org limit and re-verify. Shows an asserted signal the AWS API doesn't echo.
- [Lab 3 — Trust Policy Missing sts:TagSession](/docs/labs/lambda-microvm/missing-tagsession.md): A least-privilege MicroVM execution role whose trust policy lacks sts:TagSession. One control fires; add TagSession and re-verify to zero. Shows a single-control test in isolation.
- [Lab 2 — Over-privileged Execution Role](/docs/labs/lambda-microvm/overprivileged-execution-role.md): Plant an over-privileged MicroVM execution role (s3:*, secretsmanager:*, iam:PassRole) with a trust policy missing sts:TagSession, detect it with two built-in controls, remediate to least privilege, and re-verify to zero findings.
- [Lab 5 — Public Artifact Bucket](/docs/labs/lambda-microvm/public-artifact-bucket.md): The S3 bucket holding a MicroVM image's source (Dockerfile + code zip) has Block Public Access off and versioning disabled. Two supply-chain controls fire; enable PAB + versioning and re-verify to zero.
- [Lab 7 — Secrets Baked Into the Snapshot](/docs/labs/lambda-microvm/secrets-in-snapshot.md): An image whose init code loads a secret at module scope, so it's baked into the Firecracker memory snapshot and persists in every MicroVM launched from it. One control fires; defer secret loading to a runtime hook and re-verify.
- [Using Stave as a Go Library](/docs/labs/library-in-process.md): Run the full Stave pipeline in-process from your own Go program — no CLI, no JSON parsing.

- [Now Run Stave](/docs/labs/now-run-stave.md): Run the same S3 fixtures through Stave and compare the findings to your answers.
- [Scaffolding Controls with the Policy Forge](/docs/labs/policy-forge.md): Learn how to create a new security control with test fixtures in under
- [Tutorial: Your first multi-engine analysis](/docs/labs/reasoning-engines.md): A guided walkthrough: take one snapshot, export Stave's fact base, run three different reasoning engines (CEL, Z3, Soufflé) against it, and read each verdict.
- [S3 Public Exposure & Long-Lived IAM Keys](/docs/labs/s3-public-exposure-long-lived-iam-keys.md): A hands-on walkthrough: capture a deployed public S3 bucket and a long-lived IAM access key as an obs.v0.1 snapshot, evaluate them with Stave's built-in controls, read every part of the findings, then remediate and re-verify.
- [S3 Ransomware Protection & Forensic Auditability](/docs/labs/s3-ransomware-protection-forensic-auditability.md): Detect a compliance-tagged backup bucket missing the three controls that decide whether you survive a ransomware deletion — versioning, Object Lock (WORM), and access logging. Read all three findings and fix-then-recapture to green.
- [SadCloud — Multi-Service Misconfiguration Sweep](/docs/labs/sadcloud-multi-service-validation.md): A hands-on walkthrough: deploy NCC Group's SadCloud — a deliberately-insecure, 22-service AWS lab — capture it as an obs.v0.1 snapshot, evaluate the whole estate with Stave's built-in controls, and read the scorecard (breadth, detection rate, and a compound attack chain) instead of a single finding.
- [Shadow Admin Compute Role Privilege Drift](/docs/labs/shadow-admin-compute-role-privilege-drift.md): Detect an EC2 backend role with service-wildcard admin grants AND a sibling role that has silently drifted past its unused-permission threshold. Read both findings, learn why exit code 3 means success, and fix-then-recapture to green.
- [Skill Track](/docs/labs/skill-track.md): Six guided exercises from build to production evaluation. Each builds on the previous.
- [Build & Verify](/docs/labs/skill-track/build-and-verify.md): Build Stave from source and verify the binary and control catalog work.
- [First Findings](/docs/labs/skill-track/first-findings.md): Run Stave against a crafted observation and read your first findings.
- [Lab Validation](/docs/labs/skill-track/lab-validation.md): Deploy a known-vulnerable lab and confirm Stave detects the documented attack path.
- [Reasoning Engines](/docs/labs/skill-track/reasoning-engines.md): Export observation facts and derive compound chains with Z3, Souffle, or Prolog.
- [Snapshot Your Account](/docs/labs/skill-track/snapshot-your-account.md): Capture a read-only snapshot of your AWS account and evaluate it with Stave.
- [Write a Control](/docs/labs/skill-track/write-a-control.md): Author, test, and verify a custom control using the forge toolchain.
- [Writing Custom Controls](/docs/labs/writing-controls.md): Step-by-step guide to writing, testing, and deploying your own Stave controls.

- [Controls Reference](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/_index.md): Complete listing of all Stave controls by service domain.
- [No Unauthorized Cross-Account Access](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/access-control/inv-s3-access-001.md): S3 bucket policies must not grant access to external AWS accounts.
- [No Wildcard Action Policies](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/access-control/inv-s3-access-002.md): S3 bucket policies must not use wildcard actions (s3:* or *).
- [No External Write Access](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/access-control/inv-s3-access-003.md): S3 buckets must not grant write or delete permissions to external AWS accounts.
- [No Authenticated-Users Read Access](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/access-control/inv-s3-auth-read-001.md): S3 buckets must not grant read access to all authenticated AWS users.
- [No Authenticated-Users Write Access](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/access-control/inv-s3-auth-write-001.md): S3 buckets must not grant write or delete access to all authenticated AWS users.
- [Public-Principal Policies Must Have Network Conditions](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/access-control/inv-s3-network-001.md): S3 bucket policies that grant access to Principal * must include network-scoping conditions.
- [Shared-Bucket Tenant Isolation Must Enforce Prefix](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/access-control/inv-s3-tenant-isolation-001.md): When a shared S3 bucket uses prefix-based tenant isolation, every app-signer identity must enforce the tenant prefix.
- [S3 Signed Upload Must Restrict Content Types](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/access-control/inv-s3-write-content-001.md): Signed upload policies must restrict allowed content types to prevent stored XSS.
- [S3 Signed Upload Must Bind To Exact Object Key](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/access-control/inv-s3-write-scope-001.md): Signed upload policies must restrict write permission to a single exact object key, not a prefix.
- [No Public ACL Modification](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/acl-escalation/inv-s3-acl-escalation-001.md): S3 bucket ACLs must not be writable by AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers.
- [No FULL_CONTROL ACL Grants to Public](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/acl-escalation/inv-s3-acl-fullcontrol-001.md): S3 bucket ACLs must not grant FULL_CONTROL to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers.
- [No Public ACL Readability](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/acl-escalation/inv-s3-acl-recon-001.md): S3 bucket ACLs should not be readable by unauthenticated users.

- [Referenced S3 Buckets Must Exist And Be Owned](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/compliance/inv-s3-bucket-takeover-001.md): Any externally referenced S3 bucket must exist and be owned by your account.
- [CDN S3 Origins Must Not Be Dangling](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/compliance/inv-s3-dangling-origin-001.md): CloudFront distributions must not reference S3 origins that do not exist.
- [Public Buckets Must Not Expose VCS Artifacts](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/compliance/inv-s3-repo-artifact-001.md): Publicly accessible S3 buckets must not contain .git/ or .svn/ directories.
- [Encryption at Rest Required](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/encryption/inv-s3-encrypt-001.md): S3 buckets must have server-side encryption enabled.
- [Transport Encryption Required](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/encryption/inv-s3-encrypt-002.md): S3 buckets must enforce HTTPS via a deny policy on aws:SecureTransport=false.
- [PHI Buckets Must Use SSE-KMS with Customer-Managed Key](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/encryption/inv-s3-encrypt-003.md): S3 buckets tagged with data-classification=phi must use SSE-KMS encryption with a customer-managed key.
- [Sensitive Data Requires KMS Encryption](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/encryption/inv-s3-encrypt-004.md): S3 buckets with non-public data classification must use SSE-KMS encryption with a customer-managed key.
- [Data Classification Tag Required](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/lifecycle-governance/inv-s3-governance-001.md): S3 buckets must have a data-classification tag to enable sensitivity-gated safety checks.
- [Retention-Tagged Buckets Must Have Lifecycle Rules](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/lifecycle-governance/inv-s3-lifecycle-001.md): S3 buckets tagged with data-retention must have at least one enabled lifecycle rule.
- [PHI Buckets Must Not Expire Data Before Minimum Retention](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/lifecycle-governance/inv-s3-lifecycle-002.md): PHI buckets must not have lifecycle expiration before 2190 days (6 years HIPAA minimum).
- [Compliance-Tagged Buckets Must Have Object Lock Enabled](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/lifecycle-governance/inv-s3-lock-001.md): Buckets tagged with a compliance framework must have S3 Object Lock enabled for WORM protection.
- [PHI Buckets Must Use COMPLIANCE Mode Object Lock](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/lifecycle-governance/inv-s3-lock-002.md): PHI buckets with Object Lock must use COMPLIANCE mode, not GOVERNANCE mode.
- [PHI Object Lock Retention Must Meet Minimum Period](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/lifecycle-governance/inv-s3-lock-003.md): PHI buckets with Object Lock must have retention of at least 2190 days (6 years HIPAA minimum).
- [Versioning Required](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/lifecycle-governance/inv-s3-version-001.md): S3 buckets must have versioning enabled to protect against accidental deletion.
- [Backup Buckets Must Have MFA Delete Enabled](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/lifecycle-governance/inv-s3-version-002.md): S3 buckets tagged with backup=true must have MFA delete enabled to prevent unauthorized permanent deletion.
- [Access Logging Required](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/logging/inv-s3-log-001.md): S3 buckets must have server access logging enabled.
- [No Public Write via ACL](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-acl-write-001.md): S3 bucket ACLs must not grant write access to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers.
- [Public Access Block Must Be Enabled](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-controls-001.md): S3 buckets must have the public access block fully enabled with all four settings.
- [Complete Data Required for Safety Assessment](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-incomplete-001.md): S3 bucket safety cannot be proven when policy or ACL data is missing from the snapshot.
- [No Public S3 Bucket Read](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-public-001.md): S3 buckets must not allow public read access via policy or ACL.
- [No Public S3 Buckets With Sensitive Data](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-public-002.md): S3 buckets tagged with sensitive data classifications must not allow any public access.
- [No Public Write Access](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-public-003.md): S3 buckets must not allow public write or delete access.
- [No Public Read via ACL](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-public-004.md): S3 bucket ACLs must not grant read access to AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers for PHI data.
- [No Latent Public Read Exposure](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-public-005.md): S3 buckets must not have latent public read exposure masked only by Public Access Block.
- [No Latent Public Bucket Listing](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-public-006.md): S3 buckets must not have a latent public listing exposure masked only by Public Access Block.
- [No Public Read via Policy](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-public-007.md): S3 bucket policies must not grant public read access via Principal * with read actions.
- [No Public List via Policy](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-public-008.md): S3 bucket policies must not grant anonymous object listing via Principal * with list actions.
- [No Public S3 Bucket Listing](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-public-list-001.md): S3 buckets must not allow anonymous listing of objects.
- [Anonymous S3 Listing Must Be Explicitly Intended](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-public-list-002.md): Anonymous bucket listing increases exposure surface and must be explicitly tagged as intended.
- [Protected Prefixes Must Not Be Publicly Readable](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-public-prefix-001.md): S3 bucket prefixes marked as protected must not be publicly readable.
- [No Public Website Hosting with Public Read](/docs/reference/invariants-reference/public-access/inv-s3-website-public-001.md): S3 buckets with static website hosting enabled must not also have public read access.
